verdict.rationale: Reader exposes `auto` modes that let the service choose its own configuration: `x-engine: auto` picks between headless Chrome and lightweight curl, and `x-proxy: auto` routes through a rotating proxy pool that handles anti-bot challenges. Nothing in the evidence says these modes optimize for cost or try the cheapest option first and escalate only on failure, so the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented cost-aware auto-selection, cheapest-first fallback or escalation semantics, any pricing or token-cost linkage to engine or proxy choice, and independent corroboration.
